name: Counterfactual Effect Antichain
central_result: CEA matched perfect resolved correctness in a 150k synthetic proxy, matched the strongest conventional compiled machine on known-provider correctness/observation cost, and uniquely resolved a declaratively specified OOD provider without code changes, at the cost of higher Python decision latency and ~2.04x serialized recovery-state bytes.
counterhypothesis: PARTIALLY_SURVIVES: precompiled conventional machine is simpler/faster and equivalent on known providers.
next_falsifier: On a harmless reversible provider fixture on the accepted target VPS, inject a timeout after request dispatch but before durable local outcome, then compare CEA vs a conventional provider-specific reconciler under exact current request/auth/reservation/provider-contract identities. Measure duplicate effects, unresolved rate, provider reads, p50/p95/p99, CPU/RAM, crash/restart, stale evidence rejection, and verified outcome -> UnifiedDB re-entry -> DONE.
